I got dropped for this song. Now it’s my first Gold record. This is your reminder to trust yourself even when nobody else gets it. The label said this song would never work. They didn’t understand what I was doing. I was dropped and released it independently. For the first year and a half it didn’t stream well. It didn’t get playlists. It didn’t fit an algorithm or a genre. On paper it looked like a failure. But people slowly found it. Shared it. Passed it around. It took time. And that’s the lesson. Not everything is meant to go viral right away. Some things need to time to grow. Sometimes the rest of the world needs to catch up with you. It can feel lonely at times. I’ve felt crazy, I’ve felt sad, but that thing that makes you different is often the thing you’re meant to protect. Not fix. Everyone has opinions. Everyone is right and wrong at the same time. The only voice you actually have to learn to listen to is your own inner compass. Keep faith in yourself. Keep faith in God. Keep faith in the universe. Even when you can’t see the results yet, your belief is doing more than you think. Your thoughts, your heart, your vision are shaping reality in real time. If you’ve been given a desire, a feeling, a calling in your soul, it isnt random. It was placed there by God for a reason. Trust it. Keep going. Learn how to see in the dark. Part 2 of “The Mirror Session” with Calum Hood from 5 Seconds of Summer is now available. 🪞  What are The Mirror Sessions? Much of my journey as a musician has been intertwined with friends who are also in the world creating. The exploration of self can often happen when alone, but some of the deepest conversations in life happen when simply taking a walk with a friend. We are all reflections of each other in many ways and hearing the perspectives of those around us can have a profound impact on our path to understanding and trusting who we are. The Mirror Sessions are a place where I talk freely with close friends and acquaintances about music, art, humans and the meaning of life.
